newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares open mixed, bank shares to the fore.
newsitem.headline: German shares open mixed, bank shares to the fore.

text.p: German shares opened bourse trade mixed on Monday, as selective buying interest focused especially on financial stocks left the market unexpectedly resilient to Wall Street's decline on Friday.

The blue chip DAX index was down 0.84 points at 2,997.40 points in early dealings, but the IBIS DAX index, which tracks all-day electronic trade, was up some 12 points from its closing level late Friday afternoon.
March DTB DAX futures were up 14 points at 3,006.5 points.

Dealers expected the market to remain rangebound, with some predicting the DAX could even touch once again off the magical 3,000 point level, but said volumes were too modest for any significant gain or drop.

"This (current level) looks to me to be about the limit for today," said one dealer. "This is being supported by some isolated big orders and banks are in demand but the overall interest is pretty minimal."
Banks, which have been the focus of interest after some recent portfolio switches, were benefiting particularly from expectations of dividend announcements this week.
Deutsche Bank AG's supervisory board meets tomorrow, an event usually followed by a dividend announcement, and Commerzbank is to reveal its 1996 dividend in the morning.
Deutsche was up 1.08 marks at 85.43 marks while Commerzbank was up 35 pfennigs at 43.90 marks.
Steelmaker Thyssen AG was up 1.50 marks at 292 marks, after the company issued full 1995/1996 results and said the overall outlook was positive.
The broader market was likely to remain muted ahead of key U.S. data due on Tuesday, dealers predicted. U.S. unemployment costs are due at 1330 GMT on Tuesday.
